programme: no coherent module: the twelve concordant factors span unrelated families with no shared complex — BTG2 and HTATIP2 are independent p53-linked growth-arrest/apoptosis effectors, BRD4 is a BET bromodomain chromatin reader, FOSL2 is an AP-1 subunit, MAML1 is a Notch coactivator, ERF is a Ras/MAPK-repressed ETS factor, RFX1 drives MHC-II expression, ASH1L is an H3K4 methyltransferase, HOXA7/PAX8/FOXN1 are developmental homeodomain/paired-box/forkhead factors, and ZNF160 is uncharacterized
role_in_a: individually, several factors (BTG2, BRD4, FOSL2, PAX8) have direct bladder-cancer literature — growth suppression, chromatin-driven proliferation, and prognostic association — but nothing ties them into one process specific to this disease
role_in_b: no factor in this list has an Open Targets association with Cardiovascular_Disease, and none of the retrieved papers address cardiovascular tissue, vascular biology, or cardiac phenotypes at all
shared_axis: none can be responsibly stated: the target sets overlap only at generic proliferation/EMT nodes (MYC, TERT, EGFR, CDH1, CCND1, TGFB1) that are exactly the kind of signal the tissue-generic filter is meant to strip, and no retrieved evidence places any of these factors in cardiovascular tissue.
reasoning: The twelve factors do not form a nameable complex or pathway the way the ISGF3 example does — they belong to at least seven distinct regulatory families with no documented physical or pathway relationship among them. Every Open Targets query for Cardiovascular_Disease returned nothing for every factor, and every literature hit that exists (BTG2, BRD4, FOSL2, PAX8) is bladder-cancer-only, so there is no independent placement of this set on the cardiovascular side to reason from.
support: PMID 25284287 — BTG2 induced via Sp1/DNA methyltransferase inhibition in bladder cancer invasion, bladder-only; PMID 29239139 — BTG2 as p53/PTEN-induced tumor suppressor in bladder carcinoma cells, bladder-only; PMID 36733715 — BRD4 PROTAC degrader lethal to bladder cancer cells, bladder-only; PMID 33230453 — circNR3C1 blocks BRD4/c-myc axis in bladder cancer, bladder-only; PMID 34041036 — FOSL2 copy-number variation as bladder cancer prognostic signature, bladder-only; PMID 35154515 — circRNA/miR-326/PAX8 axis in bladder cancer progression, bladder-only. None of these six touch cardiovascular disease or vascular tissue.
how_to_falsify: Take vascular or cardiac tissue (endothelial cells, smooth muscle cells, or myocardium under stress) and test by ChIP-seq/co-IP whether BRD4, FOSL2 and MAML1 (the three with the most plausible chromatin/signaling link) co-occupy or physically associate at a shared set of target promoters, and check whether any of the twelve loci carry cardiovascular-disease GWAS signal. If co-occupancy or genetic association is found, the 'no shared axis' call here is wrong and should be revisited.
caveats: The 200 patient-group comparisons are drawn from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the comparisons are not 200 independent replications — concordance counts should be read as replicate-heavy, not as 200 separate confirmations. All twelve factors show zero Open Targets signal for Cardiovascular_Disease, which is itself informative: this pair's cardiovascular side is essentially unvalidated in the external record. The tissue-generic exclusion list (FOS, ID2, ESR1, FOXO3, TFE3, STAT5B, GFI1B, PBX1, KLF6, AR, TFEC, LITAF) removed several factors — immediate-early and nuclear-receptor regulators — that might otherwise have supplied a more recognizable stress/proliferation module; their removal is why the surviving set reads as fragmented rather than a sign a story was missed. The single-view exclusions (POU3F4, ZNF350, XPC, etc.) are unrelated to this account and don't change the conclusion.
